STEAM is an educational framework that stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts, and Mathematics. Unlike traditional teaching methods that treat subjects in isolated compartments, STEAM integrates these five disciplines into a unified, inquiry-based learning experience. Adding the Arts (which includes visual arts, humanities, music, design, and drama) to the core technical pillars of STEM brings human empathy, design thinking, and creative expression into problem-solving.
STEAM stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics.
STEAM education combines science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics to help students learn through practical activities, creativity, and problem-solving.
STEAM education helps students develop creativity, logical thinking, teamwork, and problem-solving skills through practical learning.

commands.key: what are the five components of steam

Robotics is a field of technology that involves designing, building, programming, and operating robots.
A robot is a machine that can perform tasks automatically or through programmed instructions and control systems.
Robots use sensors to collect information, controllers to process it, and motors or actuators to perform actions.
Coding is the process of writing instructions that tell a computer or robot what to do.
Learning robotics helps students understand programming, electronics, engineering, logical thinking, and real-world problem-solving.
Experiential learning is a learning approach in which students gain knowledge and skills through hands-on activities, experiments, projects, and reflection.
Innovation means developing new ideas, methods, or products, or improving existing ones to solve problems.
Technology is the use of scientific knowledge, tools, and systems to solve problems and make tasks easier.
Engineering is the process of designing, building, and improving machines, structures, and systems to solve practical problems.
Science is the systematic study of the natural world through observation, experimentation, and evidence.
Mathematics is the study of numbers, patterns, shapes, quantities, and logical relationships.
